questions.q: 2-Methylpropene reacts with HBr in the presence of benzoyl peroxide. The product is:
questions.explain: With peroxide HBr adds by a radical chain, so Br ends up on the carbon with more hydrogens. Without peroxide the Markovnikov product 2-bromo-2-methylpropane forms.

questions.q: Which reaction gives an anti-Markovnikov product?
options: Propene + HCl in the presence of peroxide
Propene + HI in the presence of peroxide
Propene + HBr in the absence of peroxide
Propene + HBr in the presence of peroxide
questions.explain: The peroxide effect applies only to HBr. HCl and HI follow Markovnikov's rule even with peroxide, giving 2-halopropanes.

questions.q: Why does HCl not show the peroxide effect?
options: The H–Cl bond is strong, so the carbon radical cannot easily abstract H from HCl
The chlorine atom is too weak an attacker to add to the C=C bond
Chlorine atoms cannot be formed from HCl
questions.explain: Both propagation steps must release energy; with HCl the H-abstraction step is endothermic because H–Cl is strong. The weak-attacker argument applies to the iodine atom from HI.

questions.q: In the peroxide-initiated addition of HBr to propene, the regiochemistry is decided by:
options: H⁺ adding to C-1 to give a secondary carbocation
Br• adding to C-2 to give a primary carbon radical
Br• adding to the terminal CH₂ to give a secondary carbon radical
Br⁻ attacking a bridged bromonium ion
questions.explain: Br• adds where it leaves the more stable 2° radical, and H is added last from another HBr, so Br ends on C-1. No carbocation forms, so there is no rearrangement.
